en: The Dyad on "Not Having a Cause but Having a Cause" (Nahetusahetukaduka) and the Triad on "Visible" (Sanidassanattika)

Dependent on a state that is not a root, not accompanied by a root, and not visible or impinging, there arises a state that is not a root, not accompanied by a root, and is visible and impinging, by way of root condition. (Under root condition: one.

Dependent on a state that is not a root, not accompanied by a root, and not visible or impinging, there arises a state that is not a root, not accompanied by a root, and is visible and impinging, by way of root condition … one.
(Abbreviated. Under root condition: three; under predominance condition: three … pe … under non-disappearance condition: three.

Dependent on a state that is not a cause, not accompanied by a cause, and non-demonstrable-with-resistance … there are three [results]. (Abbreviated. Under the root condition, three; under the predominance condition, three … pe … under the mutuality condition, one … pe … under the non-disappearance condition, three.

Dependent on a state that is not a cause, not accompanied by a cause, and non-demonstrable-and-non-resistant, a state that is not a cause, without a cause, and non-demonstrable-and-non-resistant arises by way of the root condition.
(Abbreviated. Under the root condition, one; under the predominance condition, one … pe … under the non-disappearance condition, one.
